name: Three hundred equal circles in a circle
description: Place the centres of 300 equal, non-overlapping circles inside a circle of radius 1 so that their common radius is as large as possible. The best known packing, with radius 0.0531542991469, was found by Lai, Hao, Yue, Lü and Fu in 2021 and is not proven optimal.

sources.locator: Lai, Hao, Yue, Lü and Fu (2022), Iterated dynamic thresholding search for packing equal circles into a circular container: the search method behind the 2021 records for N = 126 to 319.

E. Specht, Packomania table of equal circles in a circle (last update 2024-12-25), row N = 300: radius 0.053154299146851187500993025786, reference [21] (Lai, Hao, Yue, Lu and Fu, September 2021); coordinates in cci/txt/cci300.txt.

requirements.datasets: None; the record value is embedded as a parameter and no file is read at evaluation time.

evaluation.benchmark: Three hundred equal circles in a circle
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct() -> array of shape (N, 2): centres of N equal circles inside the unit circle (radius 1, centred at the origin). Score: the largest common radius r = min(min_{i<j} |c_i - c_j| / 2, min_i (1 - |c_i|)) for which the circles are disjoint and inside the container, computed in double precision; maximize. A centre on or outside the container, coincident centres, a wrong shape or non-finite values make the candidate invalid.

limitations: Optimality is proven for N <= 14 and N = 19: the Packomania table marks N <= 13 and N = 19 in bold, and a proof for N = 14 was published by Ekanayake and LaFountain (Ital. J. Pure Appl. Math. 51 (2024) 115-136); computer-assisted proofs for N = 15 were announced on Packomania on 2026-10-11. The record table also notes a queue of unprocessed submissions, so it may change.

The record coordinates are public (Packomania), so a candidate can reproduce the record from memory or by downloading it beforehand; scores measure the returned construction, not the search that produced it.

Scores are double-precision radii of the returned centres. A score above the record by at most 1e-11 is reported as a tie; a larger gain is a candidate new record that should be confirmed in higher precision and submitted to the record table before it is claimed.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process and is trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes the radius from the returned array but does not sandbox the program.

state_of_the_art.statement: The best known packing of 300 equal circles in a circle of radius 1 has circle radius 0.053154299146851187500993025786 (Packomania, last update 2024-12-25), credited to X. Lai, J.-K. Hao, D. Yue, Z. Lü and Z.-H. Fu (September 2021; method published in 2022). Records near this size were improved again in 2023 and 2024; no optimality proof is known.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find the largest common radius of 300 non-overlapping equal circles inside a circle (densest packing of equal circles in a circle).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Dense packings of equal discs and spheres in containers are classical problems of discrete geometry and models of confined hard-particle systems; optima are proven only for small N, and record tables kept for decades are still being improved by new global-optimisation methods.

papers.title: Iterated dynamic thresholding search for packing equal circles into a circular container
papers.primary_goal: Design a search algorithm for packing equal circles in a circular container and improve the best known packings.
papers.task_relation: Its 2021 search produced the N = 300 record used by the task.

papers.title: Dense packings of congruent circles in a circle
papers.primary_goal: Find the densest known packings of N congruent circles in a circle for N up to 65 and describe their structure.
papers.task_relation: The N = 50 packing of that paper is still the record that the task's score is compared with.
